subject: Genetics
title: Ancient DNA
description: A fast breakdown of Ancient DNA for builders.

hook.text: In 2010, scientists sequenced DNA from a 40,000-year-old Neanderthal bone. The dead can still tell secrets.

buildup.text: Svante Pääbo pioneered ancient DNA extraction. He won the Nobel Prize in 2022 for sequencing the Neanderthal genome.

discovery.text: The oldest recovered DNA is over 1 million years old, from a mammoth tooth frozen in Siberian permafrost.

twist.text: DNA degrades fast in warm climates. We may never recover ancient DNA from tropical regions. Africa's history is harder.

climax.text: Ancient DNA revealed that humans and Neanderthals interbred. Non-African humans carry 1-4% Neanderthal DNA today.

punchline.text: The dead speak through their DNA. If it survives.

quiz.question: Who won the Nobel Prize for sequencing the Neanderthal genome?
